brief: A soldering station for my bench: a holder for the iron while it is switched on and hot, plus two bins for solder and spare tips.

requirements.requirement: Holder for soldering iron while switched on and hot
requirements.evidence: Not built - 3D-printed plastic cannot safely hold a hot/energized soldering iron; would melt, risk burns/fire. System rule requires declining unsafe hot-tool holder. User should use commercial metal/ceramic stand.

finish.summary: Built two-bin organizer for solder and spare tips on 3-cell base; declined hot iron holder as unsafe in plastic, recommending metal stand instead. Outcome compromise.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text:
Declining the hot-iron holder — 3D-printed Hex Cluster is plastic and not heat-safe for a live iron. Built a safe compromise for the cold storage part instead.

**What I built:** a 3-cell L-shaped bench station with two full-depth bins ( `bin:0,-1,0~hex-bin-full` and `bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full` ) — one staged with a solder reel, one with small-parts heap as spare-tips example. Structure capped and joint-bolted, mesh clash clear. No hot holder added because it would be unsafe to use.

For a hot iron, use a commercial metal/ceramic soldering-iron stand with a heat-proof rest — not a printed plastic holder — and place it next to this caddy.
